title: 2022 HMMT February Guts Problem 7
statement: A jar contains 8 red balls and 2 blue balls. Every minute, a ball is randomly removed. The probability that there exists a time during this process where there are more blue balls than red balls in the jar can be expressed as \(\frac{a}{b}\) for relatively prime integers \(a\) and \(b\). Compute \(100 a+b\).

solutions.text: One can show that the condition in the problem is satisfied if and only the last ball drown is blue (which happens with probability \(\frac{1}{5}\) ), or the blue balls are drawn second-to-last and third-to-last (which happens with probability \(\frac{1}{\binom{10}{2}}=\frac{1}{45}\) ). Thus the total probability is \(\frac{10}{45}=\frac{2}{9}\).
